sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Fayette County
sections.html:
Fayette County deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds inside the courthouse, 16755 Highway 64, Suite 108, Somerville, TN 38068. The mailing address is P.O. Box 99 in the same town, and the phone is 901-465-5251. The register is an elected official serving a four-year term.

What the office does is record, index and store real estate and business papers: deeds, property transfers, mortgages and liens. What it does not do is write them. Documents must arrive ready to record, and staff will not tell you whether a paper is legally valid. When a title company handles your sale, you may never visit the counter, but it pays to know where the lines are.

Fees can be paid several ways, and plastic is not among them.

An out-of-town buyer who plans to walk a deed in on closing day should bring one of the accepted forms. The register's FAQ adds these handling rules:

  • Only original, signed, notarized documents are recorded, except a certified copy of something already recorded in another government office
  • The notary seal goes near the notary's name, after each signature and acknowledgment
  • The deed must show the preparer's name and address, and since April 11, 2012 it may appear anywhere in the document
  • Originals go back to whoever brought or mailed them, because the office keeps none
  • The mortgage company files a release of lien once the loan is paid off

Staff will not search title for liens or other encumbrances, but they will check the status of a specific release or assignment on request. Wills that were never probated are not kept as recorded documents. A probated will from another county or state can be recorded here if the person owned land in Fayette County.

The state charges $0.37 on every $100 of the sale price or value. It falls on the buyer at recording, and a seller usually just sees the line on the closing paperwork. Your deed and contract set the real number.

Fayette's register asks for an oath of consideration on each transfer, unless the deed cites a Tennessee statute that makes the transfer exempt, such as a divorce or the creation of a tenancy. The sworn amount stays on file, and staff can tell anyone what it was. That is how people look up a recorded sale price.

sections.h2: How a recording works from start to finish
sections.html:
In a typical sale, the title company or closing attorney carries the signed deed to the register. Staff look at the paper to see that it can be accepted, collect the fees and any transfer tax, add it to the index under the grantor and grantee names, and give back the original to whoever brought or mailed it. The office keeps no originals, so make sure the person who gets the deed back knows to store it safely.

If you are handling things yourself, bring the original signed and notarized deed, the owner and taxpayer addresses, the parcel number, the name and address of the preparer, and one accepted form of payment. Mail works too: send the document to P.O. Box 99 with a check and ID details as the office requires. When a paper is turned away for a missing item, the fix is usually small, but it can delay a closing, so run through the checklist in the next section before you sign.

Once recorded, ask staff for the date, volume and page. Keep that note with your closing file. If your buyer is paying with a loan, the lender's deed of trust is recorded at the same visit, and your old lender's release follows after payoff.

sections.h2: What the register needs on a deed
sections.html:
State law lists what a deed must contain. The register checks that the paper is acceptable and leaves its legal effect to the drafter. The checklist below comes from the University of Tennessee county training guide.

  • Legible text and an authenticated signature (T.C.A. 66-24-101 and 66-22-101)
  • Owner and taxpayer names and addresses (66-24-114)
  • A derivation clause pointing to the prior deed (66-24-110)
  • The preparer's name and address (66-24-115)
  • A parcel identification number (66-24-122)
  • Payment of fees and any transfer tax

The deed indexes run by grantor and grantee name. If you have an address but no name, call the Fayette County Property Assessor at 901-465-5226 to learn the taxpayer on a parcel. Subdivision plats are held at the register's office and show lot size, setbacks and easements as recorded, though a plat is no substitute for a survey.

Surveys are not recorded documents. For acreage, the assessor can supply tax and aerial maps, but these are drawn from the description in your deed and are not official surveys. If you own rural land and are unsure of the lines, hire a surveyor before you sign a contract that states acreage.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Fayette County
sections.html:
Fayette County sits east of Memphis, in the Memphis metro area, and Somerville is the seat. About 45,071 people live there, 8.0 percent more than in 2020. Owners live in about 81.4 percent of homes. Typical home value is $340,800 and typical gross rent is $902. Builders took out 356 permits in 2025.

Growth has moved west. Since Highway 64 was widened to four lanes in the early 1990s, Oakland has outgrown the county seat as Shelby County workers look for cheaper housing. Agriculture remains the backbone of the local economy, so acreage parcels turn up often.

The register runs a Property Fraud Alert system that notifies owners when something is recorded against their property or business. Sign-up is through a link on the register's services page. Do it before you list, since the alert flags a filing you did not make before it turns into a problem.

When the sale is done, make sure two papers reached the register: your buyer's deed and the release of your old deed of trust. The mortgage company files the release once you are paid off, and you can ask for a copy. Call 901-465-5251 for the date, volume and page of any recorded document. Staff can also say whether a release of a deed of trust has been attempted, though they make no legal claim about whether it is accurate.

sections.h2: Property tax and the closing date
sections.html: Recording and property tax are handled by different offices. Before closing, ask the county trustee and the assessor (901-465-5226) about the current bill and the valuation, so the title company is not surprised by a balance on the day. Bring the deed you took title under, a photo ID and your payoff letter if a loan is being released.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Fayette County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 901-465-5251. The office is in the courthouse at 16755 Highway 64, Suite 108, Somerville. Mail goes to P.O. Box 99, Somerville, TN 38068.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees by credit card in Fayette County?
faqs.a: No. Cash, a check with ID or a money order will work. Credit and debit cards are not taken.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not draw up documents and makes no claim that one is legally valid. Bring a deed that is signed, notarized and complete.

faqs.q: How do I find who owns a Fayette County parcel if I only have an address?
faqs.a: Call the Fayette County Property Assessor at 901-465-5226. Because the register's indexes run by name, the assessor can give you the taxpayer first.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax on a Fayette County house sale?
faqs.a: The rate is $0.37 per $100 of price or value, and the buyer pays at recording. Check your settlement statement for the exact figure.
